title: Two hours and fifty-six minutes
note: TIMES FROM AAIASB REPORT 11/2006 · LOCAL TIME (UTC+3)

events.text: Helios 522 lifts off from Larnaca, bound for Athens.
The warning horn sounds at 12,040 ft cabin altitude. It is tonally identical to the ground-only takeoff-configuration horn.
Captain Merten radios Helios operations about the "takeoff configuration warning". The engineer asks whether the pressurization panel is set to AUTO; Merten asks about circuit breakers instead.
The aircraft levels at about 34,000 ft on autopilot and continues its programmed route.
Enters the Athens flight information region with no radio contact.
Enters a holding pattern at the KEA VOR, its programmed fallback.
Two Hellenic Air Force F-16s scramble from Nea Anchialos.
The F-16s intercept on the sixth holding loop: the first officer slumped, the captain's seat empty, oxygen masks dangling.
Flight attendant Andreas Prodromou enters the cockpit on portable oxygen and waves at the F-16s.
The left engine flames out from fuel exhaustion. The aircraft leaves the hold and begins descending.
The cockpit voice recorder captures five mayday calls, still on the Larnaca frequency. Athens never hears them.
The aircraft strikes hills near Grammatiko. All 121 aboard are killed.

_facts: Every event and time is from the CONFIRMED timeline in docs/planning/CLAIMS-helios522.md (EEST). The 10:12–10:50 'nineteen failed ATC contact attempts' span is left out because it is a window, not a single minute.
